jobs.title: Hedge survey volunteers
jobs.text: We need someone to count what's living in the hedges. Last volunteer counted one hedgehog four hundred times. It was the same hedgehog. He was very patient.

jobs.title: Who's been at the bins?
jobs.text: Something has been at the wheelie bins every Tuesday night. We suspect a fox. Our chair suspects the Hendersons. Settle it.

jobs.title: Blackberries wanted, no questions asked
jobs.text: The jam stall is two jars short of a scandal. Blackberries, please. Ripe ones. Not the ones by the dog walk.

jobs.title: Tea for the planning meeting
jobs.text: Three hours on the new bus shelter and we've run out of tea. Morale is at Dunkirk levels. Bring a flask.

jobs.title: Bog census
jobs.text: Peat bogs hold more carbon than all the forests in Britain. They also hold frogs. We need two frogs, roughly. Bog-type, ideally.

jobs.title: Show us a river creature
jobs.text: We're doing a talk at the primary school and the slides are just pictures of shopping trolleys. Bring a proper river creature to show the kids.

jobs.title: Judge the bonny creature contest
jobs.text: Our usual judge was bribed with a Victoria sponge. We need someone fair, strong and above cake. Bring a creature worth judging against.

jobs.title: Wassail the orchard
jobs.text: We sing to the apple trees in midwinter to wake them up. The trees don't mind. The neighbours mind. Bring sloes for the punch.

jobs.title: Molehills on the green
jobs.text: Somebody is digging up the bowling green. Ernest says it's the Russians. It's a mole. Find out what's digging, please.

jobs.title: Rabbit census
jobs.text: It's the annual rabbit count and our counter has gone to Tenerife. Pop into the Forest, east of town, and catch anything rabbity. One will do. We'll write 'loads' on the form like we always do.

jobs.title: Moths for the silk room
jobs.text: Macclesfield made silk for the whole Empire. Now we've got one sad silkworm called Graham. Help us show the kids what lives in the woods instead.

jobs.title: The Treacle Town legend
jobs.text: Legend says a cart spilled treacle on Hibel Road and the poor scooped it up. Visit the Town Hall after dark and tell us if it still smells of treacle.

jobs.title: Macc Forest is getting cheeky
jobs.text: Something in Macclesfield Forest nicked a ranger's sandwich and then looked him in the eye. Go and remind the wildlife who's in charge. Gently.

jobs.title: Bottles for the well
jobs.text: St Ann's Well flows at a steady 28 degrees. Tourists fill bottles and leave the empties. Bring some nettles for the herbal tea stall, we're diversifying.

jobs.title: Something howling in the gods
jobs.text: There's a noise in the upper circle during the matinee. The soprano blames the radiators. Catch whatever lives up the Goyt that sounds like a soprano.

jobs.title: Pick the Goyt hedges
jobs.text: The Goyt's hedges are groaning with fruit. If nobody picks them the wasps get drunk and start fights. Forage three times.

jobs.title: Is it still raining?
jobs.text: We need someone to confirm it's raining in Manchester. It always is. But procedure is procedure. Stand in the town hall's square in the rain, please.

jobs.title: Pigeons in the mill
jobs.text: The old cotton mills are full of pigeons. Heritage pigeons, the council says. Catch one so we can find out what they're on about.

jobs.title: Bog off
jobs.text: Chat Moss swallowed half the railway once. Still hungry. Win three fights out on the moss so the creatures leave the surveyors alone.

jobs.title: Ingredients for a proper scouse
jobs.text: Me grandson says scouse is just stew. He's out of the will. Bring me wild garlic for the pan, the shop stuff's too posh.

jobs.title: The chip thieves
jobs.text: A gang of gulls has had three portions of chips and a battered sausage off one pensioner. We want them caught. We want names.

jobs.title: Clear the old railway path
jobs.text: The Wirral Way's lovely but something keeps nipping the ramblers. Win three wild fights out there and we'll put your name in the newsletter.

jobs.title: Pest control on the walls
jobs.text: There's a bylaw that says you can shoot a Welshman with a bow and arrow after dark inside the walls. We don't. We just want the pigeons gone.

jobs.title: Market day sloe gin
jobs.text: Sloe gin sells itself at the Christmas market. It also sells the stallholder. Bring sloes and we'll split the profits, roughly.

jobs.title: Ley line inspection
jobs.text: The ley lines need checking at dawn. Our usual dowser is on a retreat finding himself. He's in Swindon. Climb the Tor at dawn.

jobs.title: Floods and frogs
jobs.text: The Levels flood every winter and the frogs throw a party. Bring us a bog-type for the wetlands centre display.

jobs.title: Curse tablets
jobs.text: The Romans wrote curses on lead and threw them in the spring. Mostly about stolen cloaks. Somebody's cursed our cafe. Go and look at the baths at night.

jobs.title: The Bun Defence League
jobs.text: A Mendips creature keeps pinching our buns off the delivery van. Win three fights in the Mendips and send a message.

jobs.title: Crimp inspector
jobs.text: A proper Cornish pasty is crimped on the side, not the top. Anyone who says otherwise is from Devon. Bring us a pasty from elsewhere so we can judge it harshly.

jobs.title: Arthur's back, apparently
jobs.text: Some bloke in a bedsheet keeps telling tourists he's King Arthur. Before we deal with him, deal with the wildlife on the clifftops. Three wins at Tintagel.

jobs.title: Seaweed for the Star Gazy pie
jobs.text: Tom Bawcock's Eve is coming and the pie needs garnish. The fish heads stick out of the crust, looking at the stars. It's art. Bring seaweed.

jobs.title: Ghost count, Roman edition
jobs.text: There's a legion of Roman soldiers that marches through a cellar here, cut off at the knees. Count them at night in the Minster crypt. Bring a pencil.

jobs.title: Moorland honey for parkin
jobs.text: Proper parkin needs oats, treacle and time. Our Bonfire Night batch needs heather honey too, which is not traditional, and we're not sorry.

jobs.title: Jet black and very cross
jobs.text: Whitby jet is fossilised monkey puzzle wood. There's a creature on the moors made of the stuff and it bit our apprentice. Catch it, carefully.

jobs.title: 199 steps after dark
jobs.text: Bram Stoker got the idea for Dracula here. We'd like someone to stand in St Mary's churchyard after dark looking mysterious for the brochure.

jobs.title: Chips under siege
jobs.text: The gulls on Central Pier have learnt to unzip a handbag. Catch one of the ringleaders and we'll find it a quieter pier.

jobs.title: Walk the lights
jobs.text: We need someone to walk past the Tower after dark and tell us if any bulbs are out. All of them, ideally, are on.

jobs.title: Seabirds on the Tyne
jobs.text: Puffins on the Farnes, kittiwakes on the bridge, a lad in a stag-do vest on the Swing Bridge. One of these needs catching. The bird.

jobs.title: Nobody's minding the wall
jobs.text: The Romans built it to keep the Picts out. Now it keeps sheep in, mostly. Win three fights along Hadrian's Wall for the volunteer rota.

jobs.title: Sort the Herdwicks out
jobs.text: The Herdwicks have got onto the fell road and they're blocking the bus. They don't care. They're Herdwicks. Find us a young one to lead the rest home.

jobs.title: Graphite and slate
jobs.text: We have the world's biggest coloured pencil. Now we want a slate display to go with it. Bring a slate creature to show the coach party.

jobs.title: Count the bats at the castle
jobs.text: The castle was a working prison until 2011. Now it's mostly bats. Count them at the castle after dark. They don't like flash photography, or Yorkshiremen.

jobs.title: Keep the fells safe
jobs.text: Somebody climbed Helvellyn in flip-flops again. Before we fetch him, clear the paths: three wins in the Lake District.

jobs.title: A creature with an edge
jobs.text: Sheffield steel goes all over the world. We want to show the visitors something tough as the cutlery. Iron-type, high level, no rust.

jobs.title: Wensleydale emergency
jobs.text: The cheese van is stuck behind something large in the Dales and it won't move. Win three wild fights out there and free the Wensleydale.

jobs.title: Robin's lot
jobs.text: Every summer forty blokes turn up dressed as Robin Hood. We need someone to forage the forest before they eat it all.

jobs.title: The Melton question
jobs.text: Is a Nottingham pork pie as good as a Melton Mowbray one? Bring us two pork pies from elsewhere for a blind taste test. We're biased.

jobs.title: More canal than Venice
jobs.text: Birmingham has more miles of canal than Venice. Venice has better gondoliers. Bring a river creature for the canal festival.

jobs.title: Garlic, lots of it
jobs.text: We need wild garlic for the special. The customers won't notice it's wild. They'll notice it's good.

jobs.title: Raven roll call
jobs.text: Legend says if the ravens leave the Tower, the kingdom falls. One's gone missing. We think it's on Salisbury Plain having a mid-life crisis. Three wins out there.

jobs.title: A night at the theatre
jobs.text: Exit, pursued by a bear, it says. We've got no bear. We've got Derek. Come and watch the evening show at the Globe so Derek has an audience.

jobs.title: Lost sheep, again
jobs.text: Three thousand sheep on this hill and Dai has lost one. He knows which one. Don't ask how. Bring us a wool-bearing sort, kin-type.

jobs.title: Slate for the roof
jobs.text: Welsh slate roofed half the world. The chapel roof is leaking and the irony is not lost on us. Bring slate chips.

jobs.title: The baritones are hoarse
jobs.text: Rehearsals are Tuesday and Thursday and every baritone has a cold. Bring a cup of tea per baritone. There are two.

jobs.title: Something with fire in it
jobs.text: A Welsh dragon is red, proud, and slightly offended you even asked. Show us a creature with a bit of hearth in it for the flag-raising.

jobs.title: It's not raining, it's just Wales
jobs.text: We want a volunteer to walk the Ogwen valley in the rain, to prove the waterproofs work. They don't. Prove it anyway.

jobs.title: Clear the Beacons path
jobs.text: Pen y Fan is busy with soldiers training and influencers who've brought the wrong shoes. Three wins in the Beacons, please.

jobs.title: Something to sing about
jobs.text: The International Eisteddfod brings choirs from every country. One of them brought a creature that won't stop humming. Win three in the Dee Valley to settle the nerves.

jobs.title: The Afanc is blocking the aqueduct
jobs.text: Something has dammed the canal and it's got very big teeth. The tourists love it. We don't. Catch it.

jobs.title: Slate bait for the caban
jobs.text: Quarrymen used to argue politics in the caban at dinner. We still do. Bring slate chips for the hearth and we'll let you join in.

jobs.title: The Tylwyth Teg have nicked the scones
jobs.text: The fair folk took the scones again. They left a thimble. Very polite. Very annoying. Catch a fae creature so we can negotiate.

jobs.title: Starlings at dusk
jobs.text: Fifty thousand starlings roost under the pier at dusk. Count them. Don't look up with your mouth open.

jobs.title: Dolphins, please
jobs.text: Cardigan Bay has the biggest dolphin pod in Britain. Our boat trip has had a bad week. Show the tourists a tide creature before they ask for refunds.

jobs.title: Two pilgrimages to St Davids
jobs.text: Two pilgrimages to St Davids equal one to Rome, said the Pope. We need someone to check the coast path's in order. Three wins on the Pembroke coast.

jobs.title: Puffin census
jobs.text: The puffins are back and they've brought friends. Catch one for the census. They're very small and very cross.

jobs.title: Chips, cheese and curry, and a creature
jobs.text: The lads from the rugby have left and a storm creature's got in the fryer. It's lovely and crispy and it hates us. Catch a storm-type.

jobs.title: Midnight at the castle
jobs.text: The Marquess of Bute had a clock tower with a room for every planet. We'd like someone to be in the castle at night to hear it chime.

jobs.title: Anglesey is crawling
jobs.text: The ferry crowd are complaining about the wildlife on the road in. Three wins on Anglesey and the first pint's on us. Or a cup of tea. Your age, love.

jobs.title: Say hello to the fairies
jobs.text: You say hello to the fairies when you cross the Fairy Bridge, or bad luck follows. A lot of people forget. Show the fairies a fae creature, as an apology.

jobs.title: Oak for the smokehouse
jobs.text: Manx kippers are smoked over oak chippings. Our supplier's sent us hazelnuts instead. He's not well. Bring hazelnuts and we'll make it work.

jobs.title: Quick as a bike on the mountain
jobs.text: TT week is two weeks of bikes doing 200 miles an hour past a pub. We need a gale creature for the parade. Fast ones only.

jobs.title: Hay for the horses
jobs.text: The horse trams have run since 1876 and the horses still expect a carrot at the terminus. Bring us some field mushrooms for the depot cat. He's fussy.

jobs.title: Four horns, one sheep
jobs.text: The Loaghtan is a Manx sheep with four horns, sometimes six. We're one short for the show. Catch a Loaghtan, wherever they've wandered.

jobs.title: Turn the wheel at dawn
jobs.text: Lady Isabella is the biggest working water wheel in the world. She turns better if somebody's watching. Visit the wheel at dawn.

jobs.title: Tailless and proud
jobs.text: Manx cats have no tails. Ask them why and they'll look at you like you asked a rude question. Catch any kin-type for the club's open day.

jobs.title: A creature with a bit of go in it
jobs.text: The under-twelves need a mascot. The last one was a goat called Seamus. He's retired. Bring a brawn creature to show the lads.

jobs.title: Turf for the fire
jobs.text: Nothing smells like a turf fire in November. Bring peat for the parish hall and you'll be thanked at Mass.

jobs.title: Bread for the wake
jobs.text: Mrs Doyle is ninety-eight and having a living wake so she can hear the nice things. We need soda bread. Lots. She's popular.

jobs.title: The Púca is out
jobs.text: On November the first the Púca spits on the blackberries and they're no good after. We'd like the Púca caught before then, please.

jobs.title: Up the Wicklow road
jobs.text: The Wicklow road has wildlife the size of tractors. Three wins up there and the club will name a sandwich after you.

jobs.title: A quiet creature for the Long Room
jobs.text: The Long Room holds two hundred thousand books and one very old harp. We need a night creature to keep the moths off at closing.

jobs.title: Nobody from Dublin goes to Temple Bar
jobs.text: Stand in Temple Bar after dark and count how many people are from Dublin. We think it's none. Prove us wrong.

jobs.title: Fighting like Kilkenny cats
jobs.text: Two Kilkenny cats fought until nothing was left but their tails. We'd like a creature that can keep going. Three wins in the Comeraghs.

jobs.title: The witch's inn
jobs.text: Dame Alice Kyteler ran this inn in 1324, was accused of witchcraft, and legged it. Visit the inn at dusk and see if she's back.

jobs.title: Rebel produce only
jobs.text: The People's Republic of Cork has its own market, its own accent and its own opinion of Dublin. Bring wild garlic for the stalls.

jobs.title: Ring the bells
jobs.text: Tourists climb up and play the Shandon bells. Mostly badly. We need a gale creature to keep the pigeons off the four liars (the clocks).

jobs.title: A dolphin to replace Fungie
jobs.text: Fungie the dolphin lived in the harbour for thirty-seven years and then retired without a word. We need a new star. Catch a tide creature.

jobs.title: Clockwise only
jobs.text: Coaches go anticlockwise round the Ring of Kerry so they don't meet on the bends. The wildlife goes whichever way it likes. Three wins out there.

jobs.title: Seaweed for the oyster beds
jobs.text: September's the oyster festival. People wear black tie and eat them with a stout. The oysters want seaweed to sit on. Forage the Burren coast.

jobs.title: A proper Connemara
jobs.text: Connemara ponies are tough, kind and look good on a calendar. We need one for next year's. A real one.

jobs.title: I will arise and go now
jobs.text: Yeats wrote about bee-loud glades. We'd like honey from one. Bring heather honey and we'll read you a poem, whether you like it or not.

jobs.title: Surf's up at dawn
jobs.text: The best waves are at dawn and the instructors are all asleep. Go to the Strandhill surf shop at dawn and knock until someone answers.

jobs.title: The winter light
jobs.text: On the winter solstice the sun shines down the passage for seventeen minutes. Visit the tomb at dawn and tell us if it's still working.

jobs.title: Something's been at the barley
jobs.text: A barn creature is having the barley. Win three fights in the Boyne Valley and the farmers will owe you a pint each. There are nine farmers.

jobs.title: Breakfast emergency
jobs.text: An Ulster fry needs soda farls and potato bread or it's just a fry. Bring two soda farls and nobody gets hurt.

jobs.title: The bonfire rota
jobs.text: The bonfire committee has two rotas, three chairmen and one box of matches. Show us a hearth creature, so at least something's in charge.

jobs.title: Where the Mountains o' Mourne sweep down to the sea
jobs.text: The Mourne Wall is twenty-two miles long and it walls in nothing at all. The wildlife up there is fierce. Three wins in the Mournes.

jobs.title: Flax for the looms
jobs.text: Ulster linen was famous the world over. We still spin a bit. Catch a flax creature so the looms have a mascot.

jobs.title: She was fine when she left here
jobs.text: That's what we say. The tourists laugh every time. Go to the Titanic building at night and check the lights are off. We're on a meter.

jobs.title: Samson and Goliath
jobs.text: The two yellow cranes are called Samson and Goliath. A storm creature keeps sitting on Goliath. Catch a storm or iron creature, either will do.

jobs.title: Barley and patience
jobs.text: Bushmills has had a licence to distil since 1608. We're very patient people. Bring hazelnuts for the visitors' tasting board.

jobs.title: Finn McCool's stepping stones
jobs.text: Finn built the Causeway to fight a Scottish giant. He lost his nerve and dressed as a baby. True story. Catch a stone creature from the Causeway.

jobs.title: Walk the walls at dusk
jobs.text: Derry's walls were never breached. That's the whole point of them. Walk round the Guildhall at dusk and see the city lit up.

jobs.title: Gulls on the coast road
jobs.text: The coast road is the most beautiful drive in Ireland and the gulls know it. Three wins on the Antrim coast, please.

jobs.title: Midge count
jobs.text: The midges are out, and they've brought the whole family. Catch one for the forecast, and don't scratch.

jobs.title: Sugar for the tablet
jobs.text: Tablet is sugar, butter and condensed milk, boiled until your dentist weeps. Bring two tablets from the shop so we can check the competition.

jobs.title: Strip the Willow
jobs.text: Last ceilidh someone stripped the willow so hard they ended up in Fife. Show us a brawn creature for the door, in case it happens again.

jobs.title: Dark sky watch
jobs.text: Galloway is one of the darkest places in Britain. Go up the Dark Sky Hill at night and look at the stars. That's it. That's the job.

jobs.title: Raspberries for the cranachan
jobs.text: We're short on fruit for the Burns supper. Bring sloes instead. We'll tell everyone they're very dark raspberries.

jobs.title: Hairy coo wanted
jobs.text: A Highland coo is mostly fringe. We need one for the show. Brush it first.

jobs.title: Galloway's restless
jobs.text: The ferry crowd come off the boat and straight into the forest. Somebody has to calm the wildlife first. Three wins in Galloway.

jobs.title: Don't jump
jobs.text: The one o'clock gun has fired every day since 1861. Tourists still drop their ice creams. Stand in the castle at midday and don't jump.

jobs.title: The worst show at the Fringe
jobs.text: Our one-man show about tax law has sold four tickets. Two were my mum. Show us a fae creature for the poster, it'll help.

jobs.title: The cone on the Duke
jobs.text: There's a traffic cone on the Duke of Wellington's head. The council took it off once. The city wept. Catch an urban creature to guard it.

jobs.title: The Kelpies are watching
jobs.text: Two thirty-metre horse heads watch over the canal. They don't blink. Three wins in the Central Belt to keep them happy.

jobs.title: Up the Ben and back
jobs.text: The Ben Nevis race is up and down Britain's highest mountain in under two hours. Glencoe's wildlife keeps getting in the way. Three wins there.

jobs.title: Pick the Great Glen
jobs.text: We're doing a display of what grows in the Great Glen. So far we have heather and a crisp packet. Forage there three times.

jobs.title: Nessie sighting at dusk
jobs.text: Nessie's been spotted at dusk more than any other time. Mostly by men from Aberdeen with flasks. Visit Loch Ness at dusk. Bring a camera.

jobs.title: Something's in the water
jobs.text: A water horse keeps following the tour boat. The customers love it. The insurance company doesn't. Catch it.

jobs.title: Selkies on the shore
jobs.text: Selkies are seals that come ashore and take off their skins. Then they want them back. Catch one for the harbour master's records.

jobs.title: Stop moving the stones
jobs.text: Tourists keep building stone spirals in the Fairy Glen. The fairies hate it. Forage the glen and leave it tidy.

jobs.title: A stone for the Granite City
jobs.text: Everything in Aberdeen is grey granite that sparkles in the sun. Both sunny days. Show us a stone creature for the town house.

jobs.title: The capercaillie dance
jobs.text: Capercaillie dance at dawn and fight anyone who interrupts. We need one counted for the survey. Catch one, carefully.

jobs.title: Viking with a cold
jobs.text: Our Viking re-enactor has a cold and won't stop sneezing on the longship. Bring him a cup of tea, he says he's Norse, he's from Stromness.

jobs.title: The Ba' at Christmas
jobs.text: The Ba' is a game where half the town tries to get a ball into the harbour and the other half tries to stop them. We need a frost creature for the team photo.

jobs.title: Pickers wanted, bring a candle
jobs.text: Forced rhubarb grows in the dark and we pick it by candlelight. Something pink has been creaking in the sheds after hours. Catch it before it eats the crop.

jobs.title: Steward for the Hall of Steel
jobs.text: We need a steady pair of hands at the Royal Armouries for the school groups. Mostly it's stopping children trying on the helmets.

jobs.title: Something in the milk churn
jobs.text: A boggart has moved into the dairy and the cream keeps going off. Folk say if you flit, it flits with you. Catch the little horror instead.

jobs.title: Read to the visitors
jobs.text: Our reading volunteer has a cold. Come to the Parsonage after dark and read a chapter of Wuthering Heights by the fire. Do the voices.

jobs.title: A Spitfire for the school trip
jobs.text: Thirty Year 6s are coming to see Reginald Mitchell's Spitfire and they will not stand still. Something quick and sky-coloured would keep them busy. Show us a Gale creature.

jobs.title: Orange water, orange eels
jobs.text: The water out of the Harecastle Tunnel runs orange with iron, and the little Rustelvers love it. Catch one for our survey of the cut, gently.

jobs.title: After hours at the museum
jobs.text: Something keeps rearranging the trams in the transport gallery overnight. Our money's on a fox. Pop into M Shed after dark and have a look.

jobs.title: Chip defence
jobs.text: The Harbourside gulls have taken three pasties, a cone and a man's hat this week. Win three fights in the Avon Gorge and show them who's boss.

jobs.title: Something's crawling off the copper tips
jobs.text: A glowing lump of slag keeps crawling off the old Hafod tips at night and leaving green footprints on the engine house. Catch it before it gets into the museum.

jobs.title: Mind the flags
jobs.text: Somebody keeps knocking over the flagstone fences round the fields. We suspect something with a lot of moss on it. Catch a Dubhlet and we'll know who to blame.

jobs.title: Swell's up at the East
jobs.text: Big northerly swell forecast. Go and look at the waves off the Pentland Coast at dawn and tell us if it's working. We'd go ourselves but we're very busy waxing.

jobs.title: Something for the cheese board
jobs.text: The canteen is out of cheese and the biscuits are looking at us. The foreman says a young herdlet is good luck at the works gate. Find us one, and we'll pay in biscuits.

jobs.title: Something is eating the bait
jobs.text: Every morning the creels come up clean. We suspect a seal, a gull, or a man from Mull. Catch a tide creature and settle it.

jobs.title: Hear the cave sing
jobs.text: Visitors keep asking if Fingal's Cave really sings. Take the boat out, listen, and tell them honestly.
